scenes.tts: The first film sorted close partnerships by each partner's outcome. But how can we tell whether a root fungus really helps a plant? We need a fair comparison.
scenes.visual: Open on the first film's outcome board, then transform it into a greenhouse bench. REUSE THE FIRST FILM'S COLOUR MAP: fungus BLUE; plants GOLD; plant food YELLOW; minerals TEAL; harm RED; unaffected GREY; water pale BLUE; help is a white plus badge. A GOLD marigold rises above a pot while BLUE fungus threads approach its roots. A question mark hangs between the fungus and a blank plant-growth meter. Any graph or meter is labelled 'schematic' unless built from the lesson's data.
scenes.narration: The first film sorted close partnerships by each partner's outcome. But how can we tell whether a root fungus really helps a plant? We need a fair comparison.

scenes.visual: Title card 'Does the Fungus Help?' settles over the moving greenhouse bench. Water droplets continue falling gently into the pots.

scenes.tts: The proposed trade is clear. Fungus threads bring minerals from soil into roots. The plant passes food it made to the fungus. That suggests mutualism, but a suggestion is not a measurement.
scenes.visual: Zoom through one transparent pot. TEAL mineral dots travel along BLUE fungus threads into GOLD roots. YELLOW food dots move from the roots back into the threads. White plus badges appear beside both, then change into question marks when 'not a measurement' is spoken.
scenes.narration: The proposed trade is clear. Fungus threads bring minerals from soil into roots. The plant passes food it made to the fungus. That suggests mutualism, but a suggestion is not a measurement.

scenes.tts: Researchers grew Jubilee marigolds with living root fungus and without it. Matching pots received the same water level. The fungus was the planned difference, so plant growth could be compared fairly.
scenes.visual: The single pot duplicates into one paired comparison: left with BLUE fungus threads, right without. A water gauge cycles through on-screen labels '100%', '75%', '50%', and '25%'; these numbers are never narrated. The pair resets at each level while identical light, pot size, soil, and water lock together. Four small water icons accumulate along the bottom, keeping the frame to six main items.
scenes.narration: Researchers grew Jubilee marigolds with living root fungus and without it. Matching pots received the same water level. The fungus was the planned difference, so plant growth could be compared fairly.

scenes.tts: The experiment also tested drought. Less water reduced growth in both groups. That lets us ask whether the fungus benefit appears across the tested conditions, not just once.
scenes.visual: Water icons over the paired lanes shrink from left to right while every GOLD plant becomes shorter. The BLUE fungus remains the only planned difference within each pair. A bracket grows across all lanes labelled 'same comparison under each water level'.
scenes.narration: The experiment also tested drought. Less water reduced growth in both groups. That lets us ask whether the fungus benefit appears across the tested conditions, not just once.

scenes.tts: After growth, the shoots were cut and dried until their water was gone. Then each shoot was weighed. Drying means water in the shoots cannot confuse the comparison.
scenes.visual: A GOLD shoot lifts from each pot and moves through a simple drying cabinet labelled 'dry'. Pale BLUE droplets leave each shoot. The dried shoots settle on balances. Balance readouts appear only as changing bars, while a label reads 'mean shoot dry mass'.
scenes.narration: After growth, the shoots were cut and dried until their water was gone. Then each shoot was weighed. Drying means water in the shoots cannot confuse the comparison.

scenes.tts: What pattern would support a plant benefit from the fungus? Choose before the bars appear: higher dry mass with fungus, equal mass, or lower mass.
scenes.visual: The balances transform into paired empty bar outlines. Three large buttons appear: 'with fungus higher', 'equal', and 'with fungus lower'. The question remains above them. No table values are shown yet, so this does not answer any Predict box in the text.
scenes.narration: What pattern would support a plant benefit from the fungus? Choose before the bars appear: higher dry mass with fungus, equal mass, or lower mass.

scenes.visual: Hold the three choices. A ring fills slowly while faint greenhouse light moves across the empty bar outlines.

scenes.tts: Across the tested water levels, mean shoot mass was higher with fungus. The paired bars now use the study values shown on screen. Yet the smallest gap could be due to chance.
scenes.visual: Reuse one zero-based bar plot, showing only the current fungus/no-fungus pair. Cycle through on-screen values '5.29 / 4.44', '4.12 / 3.28', '3.06 / 2.89', and '2.62 / 2.01 g'; these numbers are never narrated. After the last pair, morph the bars into a four-dot strip of computed gaps, with no gap values or percents on screen, so the film does not answer the text's calculations. A bracket marks the smallest dot 'could be due to chance'. Caption: 'computed from table values'.
scenes.narration: Across the tested water levels, mean shoot mass was higher with fungus. The paired bars now use the study values shown on screen. Yet the smallest gap could be due to chance.

scenes.tts: Each bar is a mean, an average for a group. It does not say every plant had that mass. Group averages make the planned comparison visible.
scenes.visual: One bar opens into several small GOLD shoot icons of slightly different heights, then a horizontal mean line settles across them. The icons recombine into the bar. A label reads 'group mean, not every plant'.
scenes.narration: Each bar is a mean, an average for a group. It does not say every plant had that mass. Group averages make the planned comparison visible.

scenes.tts: Researchers also test whether a gap is larger than expected from chance variation. The smallest gap did not pass that check. The other gaps did in this study.
scenes.visual: A translucent band labelled 'chance variation — schematic' appears around the no-fungus bars. The smallest paired gap falls inside the band and receives 'not clear'. The other gaps extend beyond it and receive 'clear in this study'. Do not imply this schematic band is the paper's exact test.
scenes.narration: Researchers also test whether a gap is larger than expected from chance variation. The smallest gap did not pass that check. The other gaps did in this study.

scenes.tts: The dry-mass evidence supports a benefit to these marigolds under these greenhouse conditions. It does not show how many plants lived. It also does not measure the fungus's gain.
scenes.visual: The bars slide into an evidence card: 'plant growth: supported here'. Beside it, two empty cards appear: 'survival: not measured' and 'fungus gain: not measured here'. A border labelled 'these marigolds, this greenhouse' encloses all three cards.
scenes.narration: The dry-mass evidence supports a benefit to these marigolds under these greenhouse conditions. It does not show how many plants lived. It also does not measure the fungus's gain.

scenes.tts: Other evidence shows root fungi receive plant-made food. Combine that with the plant-growth result, and mutualism fits this case. The claim stays tied to what was tested and measured.
scenes.visual: Return to the root trade. The YELLOW food arrow into BLUE fungus gains a white plus badge. The marigold dry-mass evidence card gives the GOLD plant another plus badge. The badges join into 'mutualism fits this case', while the conditions border remains visible.
scenes.narration: Other evidence shows root fungi receive plant-made food. Combine that with the plant-growth result, and mutualism fits this case. The claim stays tied to what was tested and measured.

scenes.tts: A label is never permission to assume the outcome. Another plant, fungus, or condition may give a different result. Compare partners fairly, measure outcomes, and keep every limit attached.
scenes.visual: The mutualism label becomes a movable tag rather than a stamp. New unmeasured GOLD plant and BLUE fungus silhouettes enter under a different water icon; the tag pauses before attaching. A path writes itself: 'compare fairly', 'measure', 'state limits'.
scenes.narration: A label is never permission to assume the outcome. Another plant, fungus, or condition may give a different result. Compare partners fairly, measure outcomes, and keep every limit attached.

scenes.tts: Start with the exchange, then ask what the evidence supports for each partner. That turns help, harm, or no measured effect into a testable scientific claim.
scenes.visual: The greenhouse bench, root trade, paired bars, and evidence cards compress into the familiar outcome board. A moving pointer visits each partner before settling on the relationship label. The board remains large and fills most of the frame.
scenes.narration: Start with the exchange, then ask what the evidence supports for each partner. That turns help, harm, or no measured effect into a testable scientific claim.

scenes.visual: End card shows one line only: 'Sort symbiosis by what each partner gains or loses.' No subtitle, site name, title, or smaller line. Paired marigold bars drift faintly behind the text.
